entries.core_move: Set up the one-sided Laplace transform as $X(s)=\int_{0^-}^{\infty} x(t)e^{-st}\,dt$, identifying the lower limit, exponential weighting, and complex $s$-domain representation used for causal signal and system analysis.
Apply the $0^-$ convention when setting up one-sided Laplace transforms so discontinuities and impulses at $t=0$ are included consistently in causal signal analysis.

Compute the one-sided Laplace transform of $e^{-at}u(t)$ from the $0^-$-to-$\infty$ definition, producing $X(s)=1/(s+a)$ with convergence condition $\operatorname{Re}(s)>-a$ as the base exponential transform pair.

entries.lesson_title: Laplace Transform of the Unit Step
entries.core_move: Derive the one-sided Laplace transform of $u(t)$ as $U(s)=1/s$ by treating it as the $a=0$ case of $e^{-at}u(t)$ and checking the $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$ convergence condition.

entries.lesson_title: Laplace Transform of the Unit Impulse
entries.core_move: Compute the one-sided Laplace transform of $\delta(t)$ by using the $0^-$ convention to include the impulse at the origin and convert it into the constant $s$-domain value $1$.
Determine whether a shifted impulse lies inside the $0^-$-to-$\infty$ one-sided interval, then use sifting to convert $A\delta(t-T)$ into $Ae^{-sT}$ for $T\ge 0$.
Invert basic one-sided Laplace-domain transform pairs into causal time-domain signals by recognizing unit-step, exponential, impulse, and shifted-impulse forms under the $0^-$ convention.
